links.title: BIP 32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets (status: Deployed)
links.why: The derivation this chapter performs: the master key from the seed, the child key derivation function, hardened and normal indices, and the extended-key encoding, with the test vectors it checks against.

links.title: BIP 39: Mnemonic code for generating deterministic keys (status: Deployed)
links.why: The recovery code this chapter generates: the entropy and checksum table, the word list and the key-stretching step that turns words into a seed.

links.title: BIP 43: Purpose Field for Deterministic Wallets (status: Deployed)
links.why: Why a derivation path begins with a purpose number, which is what makes the implicit paths of this chapter readable at all.

links.title: BIP 44: Multi-Account Hierarchy for Deterministic Wallets (status: Deployed)
links.why: The five-level path - purpose, coin type, account, change, index - that most wallets still follow.

links.title: BIP 84: Derivation scheme for P2WPKH based accounts (status: Deployed)
links.why: The native-segwit path and its own test vector, one of the addresses this chapter derives and then confirms against Bitcoin Core.

links.title: BIP 93: codex32: Checksummed SSSS-aware BIP32 seeds (status: Draft)
links.why: A recovery code that is itself a share of a split secret, and carries a checksum a person can verify by hand; the most recent of the schemes this chapter compares.

links.title: BIP 329: Wallet Labels Export Format (status: Draft)
links.why: The format for the one thing a seed cannot reproduce: the labels and notes a user has attached to their own addresses and transactions.

links.title: BIP 380: Output Script Descriptors General Operation (status: Deployed)
links.why: What a descriptor is and how its checksum works; the explicit alternative to remembering a derivation path.

links.title: SLIP-0039: Shamir's Secret-Sharing for Mnemonic Codes
links.why: The scheme that splits a seed into shares, any threshold of which restores it; the secret-sharing option in this chapter's comparison.

links.title: SLIP-0044: Registered coin types for BIP-0044
links.why: The registry that says coin type 0 is Bitcoin and coin type 1 is testnet for every coin, which is what explains the one uneven row in the chapter's path table.

links.title: BIP39 test vectors (trezor/python-mnemonic)
links.why: The published vectors this chapter's recovery-code arithmetic is checked against, entropy to words to seed to master key; the English set alone holds 24 of them.

links.title: aezeed cipher seed (lnd)
links.why: A recovery code carrying a version byte and a birthday as well as entropy, which is why its holder need not scan the whole chain; one of the alternatives this chapter weighs.

links.title: Electrum Seed Version System
links.why: A code whose own words encode which wallet made it, and the cost of forging that prefix; the version-number scheme this chapter describes.

links.title: RFC 8018: PKCS #5 Password-Based Cryptography Specification Version 2.1
links.why: Where PBKDF2 is defined, with the salt and the iteration count whose purpose this chapter explains and whose cost it measures.

links.title: RFC 7914: The scrypt Password-Based Key Derivation Function
links.why: The memory-hard alternative to PBKDF2 that one of the compared schemes uses, and the parameters that set its cost.

links.title: Physical Bitcoin Attacks - Interactive Map
links.why: The running record behind this chapter's warning about coercion; its own page says the list is not comprehensive, so its count is a floor.

_note: Every link was fetched over HTTPS on 2026-10-05 from this session and answered 200; the title recorded here is the title the fetched document itself carries (for an improvement proposal, the Title line of its own preamble), not a title written from memory. A proposal's status is quoted from its preamble too, because a student needs to know whether what they are reading is deployed, draft or superseded.
